correctness.rationale: The marker at every residue b-1 equals the complement of its unique parent bit; all other sites are zero. This proves both directions of the exact parent-occurrence recursion, including the origin and all endpoint residues. The recursive factor words are unbordered by the fully inspected 2012 Lemma 5, with uniqueness from its Theorem 5.4 (explicitly not claimed new). Dilation of the exactly computed valuation-class density gives the all-position density. Isolated ones yield exactly one-or-two zero gaps and long-gap fraction 1/b. The extracted standalone checker independently matched occurrences and 56 full small-length factor classifications. All infinite assertions rest on the written proof, not finite checks.

originality.rationale: The closest same-family source (Goč–Mousavi–Shallit 2012, Theorem 5.4) establishes the number, reversal and construction of unbordered factors but not their exact positions, first starts, common densities or normalized return-gap sequence. Huang–Wen 2016 classifies return words for the classical binary b=2 sequence, so the new theorem intentionally excludes that covered base. Spiegelhofer 2021 addresses Thue–Morse gaps, not these multibase unbordered occurrences. Precise source and mathematical-record queries yielded no general b>=3 implication; incomplete indexing remains a risk.
residual_risks: A separately indexed or unindexed multibase return-word theorem might subsume the exact occurrence formula.

The 2012 factor-construction proof could make the positional result a natural derived consequence, but it does not give its all-position equivalence, natural densities or identical gap words explicitly.
The 2021 guiding source was read only to abstract depth; it is not a plausible same-family covering source.

value.rationale: Positions and long/short return gaps are natural occurrence-geometric invariants, motivated by the established two-unbordered-factor phenomenon and literature on gap sequences of automatic words. This is a full, exact, all-length and all-generalized-base classification, not an arbitrary finite slice; its universality identifies one normalized gap sequence shared by both factors across all n, plus exact densities and first occurrences. The general-base extension goes beyond existing binary return-word coverage. It is useful for locating and sampling unbordered factors and for recurrence questions.
